name: Armodafinil (Nuvigil)
summary: Wake-promoting agent for narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea–related sleepiness, and shift work sleep disorder. Off-label for idiopathic hypersomnia and MS-related fatigue. Schedule IV with rare but serious rash and psychiatric risks.
description: Armodafinil (Nuvigil) is a central nervous system stimulant–like wake-promoting agent used to improve daytime wakefulness in people with narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), or shift work sleep disorder (SWSD). It is the R-enantiomer of modafinil and generally has a longer half-life. It is taken once daily in the morning for narcolepsy/OSA or about an hour before the work shift in SWSD. Serious but rare risks include Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS), toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), multiorgan hypersensitivity (DRESS), and mood or psychotic symptoms. It is a Schedule IV controlled substance with abuse and dependence potential.
patient_summary:
Nuvigil (armodafinil) is a ‘wakefulness’ medicine that helps you feel less sleepy if you have narcolepsy, sleep apnea–related sleepiness, or shift-work sleep disorder. You usually take it once in the morning (or about an hour before your work shift). It is **not** a cure for sleep problems and does **not** replace real sleep—you still need good sleep routines and treatment of underlying conditions like sleep apnea.

Most people notice feeling more awake and focused, but some get headaches, nausea, anxiety, or trouble sleeping if they take it too late. Rarely, serious rashes (like Stevens–Johnson syndrome) or mood changes (depression, suicidal thoughts, mania, hallucinations) can happen. It’s a Schedule IV controlled substance, so there is some risk of abuse or dependence. Birth control pills can work less well while taking it, so extra contraception is needed.

primary_indications: Obstructive sleep apnea–related excessive daytime sleepiness

linked_conditions.context: Improves daytime wakefulness and reduces excessive sleepiness in narcolepsy when used with appropriate behavioral strategies.
Used to treat residual daytime sleepiness in OSA after underlying airway obstruction is adequately treated (eg, with CPAP). Does not treat the obstruction itself.
Taken about 1 hour before the night shift to improve wakefulness in people with persistent sleepiness despite nonpharmacologic measures.
Common off-label wake-promoting option, typically starting 50–200 mg in the morning and titrating based on response.
Used off-label for MS-related fatigue, usually starting at 50 mg in the morning and titrating up to 250 mg as tolerated.

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to armodafinil, modafinil, or any component of the formulation
History of severe rash or multiorgan hypersensitivity with modafinil/armodafinil

Significant structural heart disease, left ventricular hypertrophy, or mitral valve prolapse syndrome triggered by previous CNS stimulant use (relative contraindication; avoid per labeling and expert guidance)

efficacy_response.comparison_data: In open-label and controlled trials, most patients were rated as ‘much improved’ or ‘very much improved’ on global clinical scales at final visit.
efficacy_response.patient_text: In clinical studies, most people taking armodafinil for conditions like narcolepsy, sleep apnea–related sleepiness, or shift work disorder were rated by clinicians as ‘much improved’ or ‘very much improved’ by the end of treatment.

pharmacokinetics.bioavailability: High; exact percentage not firmly established but similar to modafinil.
pharmacokinetics.onset: Wake-promoting effects typically begin within a few hours of dosing.
pharmacokinetics.peak_plasma: ≈2 hours in the fasted state (later with food).
pharmacokinetics.duration_IR: Wake-promoting effects usually last throughout the daytime when taken in the morning; later dosing can interfere with nighttime sleep.
pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic; multiple pathways including amide hydrolysis and CYP3A4/5 oxidation to inactive metabolites (eg, modafinil acid, modafinil sulfone).
pharmacokinetics.protein_binding: ≈60% (primarily to albumin; based on modafinil data).
pharmacokinetics.food_effect: Food delays absorption and time to peak but has minimal effect on overall exposure (AUC). Taking with food may slightly delay onset.

sections.heading: What It's Used For
sections.text: Armodafinil is used to improve wakefulness in adults with certain sleep-wake disorders. It is **not** a substitute for adequate sleep or for treating the underlying airway obstruction in sleep apnea.
items: {link:condition:narcolepsy:Narcolepsy}: Reduces excessive daytime sleepiness and improves ability to stay awake.
{link:condition:obstructive-sleep-apnea:Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA)}: Treats residual daytime sleepiness in patients with adequately treated OSA (eg, on CPAP) who remain very sleepy.
{link:condition:shift-work-sleep-disorder:Shift Work Sleep Disorder}: Taken about 1 hour before starting a work shift to help stay awake during the shift.
off_label: Idiopathic hypersomnia (morning dosing, titrated up to 250 mg/day)
Multiple sclerosis–related fatigue (morning dosing, typically 50–250 mg/day)
Other secondary hypersomnias per sleep specialist judgment

sections.heading: What People Feel
sections.intro: People describe a mix of benefits and side effects. Experiences vary a lot depending on dose, timing, and baseline sensitivity.

quotes: I didn’t feel normal, but I felt *awake enough* to function at work.
I stopped nodding off during meetings.
It’s like someone turned the brightness up on my day.
I get a mild headache most days I take it.
Sometimes my stomach feels off—nausea or loose stools.
Dry mouth is annoying, but water and gum help.
items.note: Headache and nausea are among the most common side effects and are often dose-related.

quotes: I felt a bit more wired and anxious.
If I take it too late, I can’t fall asleep at night.
A little jittery at higher doses.
items.note: Taking it early in the day and keeping caffeine moderate can reduce jitteriness and insomnia.

quotes: I developed a rash and my doctor had me stop immediately.
My mood felt darker and more irritable on it.
My family noticed I wasn’t myself—more paranoid and edgy.
items.note: Serious skin reactions (SJS/TEN) and psychiatric symptoms (depression, suicidal thoughts, mania, hallucinations) are rare but require **immediate** medical attention.

sections.heading: How Fast It Works
sections.text: Armodafinil is designed to cover your waking period, not to act instantly like a caffeine shot.
key_points: Absorption: Reaches peak blood levels in about 2 hours when taken on an empty stomach.
Food: Taking with food delays peak a bit, so the effect may come on more gradually.
Duration: The half-life is ~15 hours, so a morning dose usually provides wakefulness benefits through the day.
Timing: To avoid insomnia, it’s usually taken in the morning (or 1 hour before the start of a shift for shift-work use).

sections.heading: How Well It Works
sections.text: In clinical trials and open-label studies, most patients taking armodafinil for narcolepsy, OSA-related sleepiness, or shift work sleep disorder were rated as ‘much’ or ‘very much improved’ on global clinical scales. Subjective sleepiness scores and objective wakefulness tests generally improve, though not all patients return to completely normal wakefulness.
sections.clinical_details: Across studies of armodafinil and modafinil, a majority of participants had clinically meaningful reductions in excessive sleepiness and functional impairment. Benefits are greatest when used as part of a comprehensive plan that includes treating underlying conditions (eg, CPAP for OSA) and optimizing sleep schedule and hygiene.

citation.title: Armodafinil in the treatment of excessive sleepiness

sections.heading: Critical Safety Information
sections.highlight: Serious, sometimes life-threatening skin reactions (SJS/TEN) and multiorgan hypersensitivity (DRESS) have been reported with armodafinil and modafinil.
other: Severe rash: Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS), toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN), and other serious reactions have occurred, sometimes after weeks of use.
Multiorgan hypersensitivity / DRESS: Fever, rash, swollen glands, and internal organ involvement; can be life-threatening.
Psychiatric symptoms: Depression, anxiety, irritability, mania, hallucinations, suicidal ideation, and aggressive behavior have been reported.
Cardiovascular risks: May increase heart rate and blood pressure; caution in structural heart disease, prior MI, or angina.
Abuse and dependence: Schedule IV with potential for misuse, particularly in people with substance use disorder history.
Not a cure: Does not replace treatment of underlying sleep disorders (like CPAP in OSA) or adequate sleep.
patient_counseling: Stop the medication and get medical help right away if you develop a rash, blisters, mouth sores, red eyes, or peeling skin—even if symptoms seem mild at first.
Contact your clinician urgently if you feel more depressed, have suicidal thoughts, new paranoia, hallucinations, mania, or major changes in behavior.
Check your blood pressure and heart rate periodically, especially if you have cardiovascular risk factors.
Avoid taking it late in the day to reduce insomnia risk.
Do not rely on this drug to make it ‘safe’ to drive when sleepy—if you still feel too sleepy, do not drive or operate machinery.
Use backup birth control (eg, condoms) while on armodafinil and for 1 month after stopping, because it can make hormone-based contraceptives less effective.

sections.heading: Side Effects
sections.summary: Most common side effects are headache, nausea, nervousness, and insomnia. Rare but serious reactions include SJS/TEN, DRESS, psychiatric symptoms, and serious cardiovascular or blood disorders.
plain_language_list: Nausea, stomach upset, diarrhea or constipation
Trouble sleeping if taken too late

common.patient_note: The most common complaint. Often manageable with hydration, dose timing, or OTC analgesics if appropriate. Persistent or severe headaches may require dose adjustment or switching medications.
Mild nausea, diarrhea, or stomach discomfort can occur, especially when starting or increasing the dose. Taking with a light snack may help, though it can delay onset slightly.
More likely when taken later in the day or at higher doses. Dosing early in the morning and minimizing caffeine can help.
Some people feel jittery, on edge, or more anxious. Lowering the dose or adjusting timing can help; serious mood changes require reassessment.
A minority feel lightheaded or paradoxically fatigued; often improves with dose titration.
Mild rash or increased sweating can occur. Any spreading, blistering, or painful rash needs urgent evaluation.

serious: Stevens–Johnson syndrome (SJS), toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN): blistering, peeling skin; mucosal sores; fever; eye redness; can be fatal.
Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS): fever, rash, swollen lymph nodes, liver or kidney injury.
Severe psychiatric reactions: depression, suicidal ideation, hallucinations, mania, aggressive or violent behavior.
Serious cardiovascular events: chest pain, arrhythmias, hypertension worsening, dyspnea, signs of heart failure.
Pancytopenia or other blood dyscrasias: easy bruising, infections, fatigue.
Significant liver injury: dark urine, jaundice, right upper quadrant pain.

sections.heading: Critical Drug Interactions
sections.intro: Armodafinil is a weak CYP3A4 inducer and weak CYP2C19 inhibitor, and a minor CYP3A4 substrate. It can lower levels of some medications (including hormonal contraceptives) and raise levels of others.

items.with: Hormonal contraceptives (pills, patch, ring, implants, some IUDs, depot injections)
items.risk: Reduced contraceptive effectiveness due to CYP3A4 induction.
items.action: Use backup or alternative contraception during treatment and for 1 month after the last dose (eg, condoms, non-hormonal IUD).

items.risk: Additive stimulant effects: increased blood pressure, heart rate, anxiety, and insomnia.
items.action: Avoid combinations when possible; if used, monitor BP/HR closely and watch for overstimulation.

items.risk: Armodafinil may lower antipsychotic levels (via CYP3A4 induction), potentially worsening psychosis.
items.action: Monitor mental status; dose adjustments to the antipsychotic may be needed.

items.with: Cyclosporine, tacrolimus, sirolimus and other CYP3A4 substrates with narrow therapeutic index
items.risk: Reduced drug levels and loss of efficacy.
items.action: Monitor levels and adjust doses as needed; in some cases, avoid the combination.

items.with: CloBAZam and other CYP2C19 substrates (phenytoin, mavacamten)
items.risk: Increased levels and risk of adverse effects of the CYP2C19 substrate.
items.action: Monitor closely and reduce substrate dose if needed.

items.risk: Alcohol may blunt therapeutic effects and add CNS side effects; sedatives may worsen mood or cognitive changes.
items.action: Avoid alcohol; use sedatives cautiously and only under supervision.

sections.heading: Stopping or Changing Dose
sections.text: Armodafinil is a Schedule IV controlled substance with some potential for abuse and dependence. Stopping abruptly after long-term or high-dose use may cause withdrawal-like symptoms.
key_points: Short-term/low-dose use: Many patients can stop without formal taper, but some may feel more fatigued or sleepy for several days.
Long-term or high-dose use: Gradual dose reduction is preferred to reduce risk of rebound sleepiness, mood changes, or rare seizures.
Abuse risk: Screen for substance use history before starting; monitor for dose escalation, compulsive use, or drug-seeking behaviors.
Switching stimulants/wake-promoting agents: Coordinate cross-titration with a sleep specialist or psychiatrist and monitor cardiovascular and psychiatric status closely.

sections.heading: Dosing Information
sections.text: Doses are individualized based on diagnosis, response, side effects, and comorbid conditions. All doses are oral and typically given once daily in the morning.

adult.narcolepsy_initial: 50–150 mg once daily in the morning.
adult.narcolepsy_titration: Increase by 50 mg/day at ≥1-week intervals as needed and tolerated.
adult.narcolepsy_max: 250 mg/day (once daily or divided morning/midday doses).
adult.osa_initial: 50–150 mg once daily in the morning for OSA-related excessive daytime sleepiness (after adequate treatment of airway obstruction).
adult.osa_titration: Increase by 50 mg/day at ≥1-week intervals up to 250 mg/day.
adult.osa_max: 250 mg/day. Doses >150 mg/day have not consistently shown additional benefit in trials.
adult.shift_work_disorder: 150 mg as a single dose about 1 hour before the start of the work shift.
adult.idiopathic_hypersomnia_offlabel: 50–200 mg once daily in the morning; can increase in 50 mg increments at ≥1-week intervals up to 250 mg/day (once or divided morning/midday).
adult.ms_fatigue_offlabel: 50 mg once daily in the morning; increase gradually as needed up to 250 mg once daily.
adult.renal: No formal adjustment; clinically significant changes unlikely as little active drug is renally excreted.
adult.hepatic_severe: Use reduced doses due to decreased clearance and higher steady-state concentrations.
adult.older_adults: Start at lower doses and titrate more slowly; exposures are ~15% higher and clearance ~12% lower in people ≥65.

sections.simple_explanation: Most people start at 50–150 mg once in the morning and slowly increase by 50 mg steps every week or so, up to a usual maximum of 250 mg per day. Taking it early in the day helps avoid insomnia. In shift work sleep disorder, a single 150 mg dose 1 hour before the work shift is common.

sections.heading: Pregnancy, Breastfeeding, Special Groups
sections.text: Armodafinil has important reproductive and special population considerations.
sections.pregnancy: Registry data (Nuvigil/Provigil pregnancy registry) suggest an increased risk of major congenital malformations (≈13%) with in utero exposure, without a specific pattern. Intrauterine growth restriction and spontaneous abortion have also been reported. Avoid use in patients who could become pregnant when possible. Evaluate pregnancy status before starting and use effective contraception if treatment is necessary.
sections.lactation: Armodafinil is present in breast milk. Limited data show measurable levels in milk; effects on breastfed infants are not well defined. The manufacturer recommends weighing the benefits of breastfeeding against the potential risk of infant exposure and the mother’s need for treatment.
sections.pediatrics: Not approved in children. Serious rashes, including SJS, have occurred in pediatric patients. Use is generally avoided.
sections.geriatrics: Older adults have higher systemic exposure and may be more sensitive to side effects (BP, HR, CNS effects). Start low and go slow.
sections.hepatic: Use with caution, especially in severe hepatic impairment where clearance is reduced and concentrations are higher; dose reduction is recommended.
sections.renal: Severe renal impairment increases exposure to inactive modafinil acid metabolite but not active drug; dose adjustment is usually not required, but clinical monitoring is advised.

sections.heading: Clinical Monitoring
items: Blood pressure and heart rate periodically, especially in patients with cardiovascular risk factors or on other stimulants.
Skin and mucous membranes for rash, blisters, or sores—particularly during the first 8 weeks.
Mental status: mood, anxiety, irritability, psychotic symptoms, suicidal ideation.
Sleepiness: degree of daytime sleepiness (eg, Epworth Sleepiness Scale) and functional outcomes; reassess regularly.
Signs of abuse or dependence: dose escalation, early refills, using more than prescribed, or drug-seeking behavior.
Adherence and timing: confirm correct morning or pre-shift dosing and avoidance of late-day doses that interfere with sleep.
In pregnancy-capable patients: contraceptive use and discussions about pregnancy planning.

sections.heading: Available Formulations
sections.text: Armodafinil is available as oral tablets in several strengths.
items: Tablets (Nuvigil brand): 50 mg, 150 mg, 200 mg, 250 mg.
Generic armodafinil tablets: 50 mg, 150 mg, 200 mg, 250 mg.

sections.heading: Mechanism of Action
sections.text: The exact mechanism is not fully understood. Armodafinil is the R-enantiomer of modafinil and primarily binds to the dopamine transporter, inhibiting dopamine reuptake and increasing extracellular dopamine in certain brain regions involved in wakefulness. It does **not** act as a direct dopamine receptor agonist and has minimal activity at most other common receptors or enzymes involved in sleep–wake regulation.

sections.heading: Place in Treatment Algorithm
sections.text: Armodafinil is a first-line or early option for excessive daytime sleepiness in narcolepsy, residual sleepiness in adequately treated OSA, and shift work sleep disorder when non-medication strategies are not enough. It is often preferred over traditional stimulants for some patients due to a somewhat lower risk of classic stimulant side effects (eg, marked tachycardia, appetite suppression), but still carries significant psychiatric, dermatologic, and cardiovascular cautions. For idiopathic hypersomnia and MS fatigue, it is a commonly used off-label agent, typically managed by sleep specialists or neurologists.

seo.title: Armodafinil (Nuvigil): Dosing, Side Effects, Rash Risk & Pregnancy Warnings
seo.description: Nuvigil (armodafinil) for narcolepsy, sleep apnea–related daytime sleepiness, and shift work sleep disorder: dosing (50–250 mg), side effects, serious rash and psychiatric warnings, pregnancy data, and contraceptive considerations.

editorial.reviewStatement: Content aligned with FDA labeling for Nuvigil, AASM guidelines for hypersomnolence disorders, and published data from the Nuvigil/Provigil pregnancy registry.

faqs.a: Nuvigil is used to improve wakefulness in adults who are very sleepy during the day because of narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), or shift work sleep disorder. It is not a cure for these conditions and does not replace adequate sleep or CPAP treatment for OSA.

For narcolepsy or OSA-related sleepiness, it is usually taken once in the morning. For shift work sleep disorder, a single 150 mg dose is typically taken about 1 hour before the work shift. Taking it later in the day can cause trouble sleeping at night.

faqs.q: What are the most common side effects?
faqs.a: The most common side effects are headache, nausea, dry mouth, dizziness, anxiety or nervousness, and trouble sleeping if taken too late. Most side effects are dose-dependent and may improve with dose adjustment or timing changes.

faqs.q: Can Nuvigil cause serious skin reactions?
faqs.a: Yes. Rare but serious skin reactions like Stevens–Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis have been reported. Any rash, blistering, or sores in the mouth, eyes, or on the skin should be treated as an emergency—stop the drug and get medical help right away.

Yes. Nuvigil can make hormone-based contraceptives (pills, patch, ring, implants, injections) less effective. You should use a backup method (like condoms) while taking Nuvigil and for 1 month after your last dose.

Nuvigil is a Schedule IV controlled substance, which means it has some potential for abuse and dependence. Most patients use it safely, but people with a history of substance use disorder should be monitored closely.

faqs.q: Can I drink alcohol while taking Nuvigil?
faqs.a: Alcohol can interfere with Nuvigil’s effects and may increase side effects like dizziness, mood changes, or poor judgment. It’s best to avoid alcohol while on Nuvigil.

Registry data suggest a higher rate of major birth defects with modafinil/armodafinil exposure in pregnancy. If you are pregnant or planning pregnancy, discuss alternative options with your prescriber. People who could become pregnant should use effective contraception and generally avoid armodafinil unless benefits clearly outweigh the risks.

faqs.q: Does Nuvigil replace CPAP for sleep apnea?
faqs.a: No. In obstructive sleep apnea, Nuvigil is only for residual daytime sleepiness after the airway obstruction is adequately treated, usually with CPAP. It does not fix the airway blockage and should not be used instead of CPAP.

faqs.q: What happens if I miss a dose?
faqs.a: If you miss a dose and it’s still early in the day, you can take it when you remember. If it’s near bedtime, skip the missed dose and take your usual dose the next day. Do not double up doses to ‘catch up,’ as that increases the risk of side effects and insomnia.
